title: Document save_ tool action-fold exception for lifecycle actions
description:
## Summary

Document an exception to the `save_` tool naming convention in the gitlab-mcp-tool-builder skill. Tools prefixed `save_` can now fold non-field-mutation lifecycle actions (like `retry` or `cancel`) behind an `action` parameter when those actions operate on the same resource the tool creates, rather than requiring a separate dedicated tool. This pattern was discovered and used while building the `save_pipeline` MCP tool in !248323. Version bumped from 1.6.1 to 1.6.2 to satisfy the skills version check.

## How to test locally

1. Run `BASE_REF=origin/master scripts/lint/check-skills-version-bump.sh` and confirm it exits with status 0.
2. Commit the change locally and verify that the pre-commit hooks pass, specifically the `skills-parity` check which confirms `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills` remain synchronized via the symlink.

title: Skip archived projects in PipelineScheduleWorker
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

`PipelineScheduleWorker` iterates `Ci::PipelineSchedule.runnable_schedules`
and enqueues `RunPipelineScheduleWorker` for every runnable schedule,
including schedules that belong to archived projects. `RunPipelineScheduleWorker`
already skips archived projects itself (added in !195638), so these enqueues
are wasted work that just gets discarded downstream.

This filters archived projects out of each batch before enqueueing.

`ci_pipeline_schedules` and `projects` live on separate databases, so this
can't be done with a single join. Instead, for each batch (bounded to
`BATCH_SIZE`), it looks up which of the batch's project ids belong to
archived projects and rejects those schedules in Ruby before calling
`bulk_perform_in_with_contexts`.

## References

- Resolves https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/609127
- Related to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/551174
- Follow-up to !195638

## How to set up and validate locally

1. In a Rails console, create a project and a pipeline schedule with
   `next_run_at` in the past:
   ```ruby
   project = create(:project, :repository)
   schedule = create(:ci_pipeline_schedule, project: project, next_run_at: 1.hour.ago)
   ```
1. Archive the project: `project.update!(archived: true)`.
1. Run `PipelineScheduleWorker.new.perform`.
1. Confirm no `RunPipelineScheduleWorker` job was enqueued for `schedule`
   (for example via `Sidekiq::Queues["pipeline_schedule:run_pipeline_schedule"]`
   in test mode, or by checking no pipeline was created).

## MR acceptance checklist

Evaluate this MR against the [MR acceptance checklist](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/code_review/#acceptance-checklist).
It helps you analyze changes to reduce risks in quality, performance, reliability, security, and maintainability.
